newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Thousands of Israelis call for peace at rally.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Israelis call for peace at rally.

text.p: Thousands of Israelis appealed to hardline Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at a Tel Aviv rally on Saturday night to end Israeli-Palestinian violence that has claimed nearly 70 lives in four days.

Organisers of Israel's "Peace Generation" organisation estimated that 20,000 people attended the rally. They carried banners which read "We want peace, not war," "Only peace will stop the bloodshed," and "Close the tunnel".
Israel Radio quoted police as saying 30,000 attended.

Netanyahu earlier in the week attended the opening of a new entrance in a tourist tunnel through a Jerusalem archaeological site, drawing world condemnation and triggering protests by Palestinians who called it an assault on nearby Moslem shrines.

Israeli peace activists at the rally promised to back the right-wing Netanyahu as long as he pursued peace, even if he chose a different path from that of his left-centre predecessors Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres, the man he replaced as prime minister in May.

"If you will go the way of peace, even if it is a little different from the ways of Peres and Rabin,...(we) will support you -- the peace camp will support you," Noam Kedem of the Peace Generation group told the crowd.

But some in the crowd, using Netanyahu's nickname, shouted: "Bibi, go home". At least one demonstrator raised a sign that read: "There's no peace. There's no security," a play on the "peace with security" promise of Netanyahu's election campaign.
Speakers urged the Israeli leader to implement the peace deals launched by Rabin and Peres in secret negotiations with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Oslo in 1993.

They said Arafat had to ensure his police held their fire if he expected Israeli support. Fourteen Israeli soldiers have died in gunbattles with Palestinian forces in the violence along with 54 Palestinians.

Retired General Shlomo Lahat, a leader of the group and a former longtime mayor of Tel Aviv, told Reuters: "The prime minister should lead the process and he should know that he must give the Palestinians a state immeidately. He shouldn't wait.
"If he has problems...they should make a unified government. He should take in Shimon Peres, and Shimon Peres will teach him how to lead the process," Lahat said.

"Last but not least a word to the Palestinians," Lahat said. "Gentlemen, if you will repeat again and shoot at our soldiers and our people, we will not be able to support you. You can talk, you can demonstrate, you can do anything. Don't throw stones to kill people and don't shoot to kill people," he added.
Yael Dayan, a member of parliament from Peres's Labour party: "I am here to say to Mr Netanyahu, my prime minister, that he has cheated, he deceived me.
"If he doesn't go on with Oslo he should go home. He is responsible and the sole one responsible for the terrible setback and regression that we are seeing in the peace talks," she said.
